\[
\begin{gathered}
\begin{pmatrix} u \\ v \end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix} \cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix} x + \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{W'}{2} \\ y + \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{H'}{2} \end{pmatrix}
+
\begin{pmatrix} \tfrac{W}{2} - \tfrac{1}{2} \\ \tfrac{H}{2} - \tfrac{1}{2} \end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\theta = 15^{\circ}
\end{gathered}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \((x, y)\): Output pixel index
- \((u, v)\): Source position in pixel-center units
- \(\theta\): Rotation angle, counterclockwise
- \(W, H\): Source width and height
- \(W', H'\): Output width and height

For each output pixel, the center is turned back by the angle into the source image. The value at that source position (u, v) is read by the chosen interpolation. Turning back, not forward, gives every output pixel exactly one value and leaves no holes. With y growing downward, this matrix turns the picture counterclockwise on screen.
